name: Kashmiri Harissa
ingredients: 1 kg mutton (boneless or on the bone)
instructions: 1. In a large heavy-bottomed pot or copper cauldron, cook mutton with salt, water, and aromatic spices until the meat becomes tender.
2. Add the soaked rice to the pot and continue to cook on low heat for several hours, stirring continuously.
3. Periodically mash the meat and rice mixture using a heavy wooden pestle to achieve a smooth, homogenous texture.
4. Heat the ghee separately until smoking hot and pour it over the mixture as a tempering (tadka).
5. Continue stirring until the mixture reaches a thick, paste-like consistency where the meat and rice are inseparable.
6. Serve hot, traditionally topped with additional hot ghee and served with fresh Kashmiri bread (tsot).
description: Kashmiri Harissa is a legendary winter delicacy in Kashmir, known for its laborious preparation process. It is traditionally prepared overnight in dedicated Harissa shops and is considered a soulful, high-energy breakfast dish served during the freezing winter months.
